summary: Disclosed remote-agent CLI: WebRTC-driven shell/PTY execution on the installer host
details: @factiii/runner is a foreground daemon (`factiii-runner start`) whose advertised function is to accept commands from Factiii's mobile/web clients over a WebRTC data channel to api.factiii.com and execute them locally as tmux sessions and agent subprocesses via node:child_process. The remote-control capability is documented in the README and in a DISCLOSURE file, is gated by an interactive pairing flow bound to a Factiii account (pairing JWT encrypted at rest in the OS keychain), uses an outbound signaling connection to api.factiii.com rather than a public listener, and starts only when the user runs the documented foreground command — there is no install/import-time auto-start, no boot persistence, and no lifecycle hook that brings the channel up. The embedded Python helper (embedder/serve.py) exposes a local HTTP endpoint used by the agent process. The capability traced matches what the package documents: remote operators paired to the installer's Factiii account can drive shells and PTYs on the installer's host, with full-host blast radius once paired. No collateral harvesting of unrelated installer secrets (~/.aws, ~/.ssh, ~/.npmrc, browser or wallet stores), no env-var scraping, no non-vendor control plane, and no second undisclosed channel were observed in the shipped bundle.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
